paper_title: Impact of 3-D Integration on Thermal Performance of RISC-V MemPool Multicore SOC

extraction.paper_title: Impact of 3-D Integration on Thermal Performance of RISC-V MemPool Multicore SOC

scenario.description: Thermal profile comparison of MemPool 2D-SOC versus 3D-SOC with Memory-on-Logic (MOL) configuration. The 2D-SOC baseline has maximum junction-to-ambient temperature Tmax of 46°C. The 3D-SOC MOL configuration shows Tmax of 55°C on memory die and 57°C on logic die, representing a 20% increase over 2D baseline. The thermal design power (TDP) is 40 W for larger workloads. Silicon technology is 28 nm.
scenario.architecture: RISC-V MemPool 256-core multicore SOC with 64 tiles, each containing 4 cores sharing 16 KiB scratchpad memory (SPM) and 2 KiB instruction cache. Die footprint 3.95 × 3.95 mm per layer. Memory die thickness 100 µm, logic die thickness 5 µm (thinned for nTSV). Face-to-face (F2F) wafer-to-wafer bonding with 6 metal layers in both tiers (M6M6) and 2.85 µm F2F via layer. Polymer TIM 100 µm thickness between dies and heatspreader.
scenario.workload: Synthetic full workload at 40 W TDP baseline for thermal design power comparison. Power breakdown: 39% cores, 27% interconnects, 13% instruction cache (I$), 11% SPM, 10% others per Figure 3.
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state thermal analysis at ambient temperature 27°C. Maximum on-chip temperature measured relative to ambient. No dynamic thermal management or active cooling control applied; passive convection resistance of 0.17 K/W between heatsink and ambient, 50 K/W between PCB and ambient.

physical_mismatches.reason: 3D integration with Memory-on-Logic (MOL) configuration introduces vertical stacking that multiplies power density by die count (2 dies), reducing die footprint by 0.665× but increasing power density by 1.37×, changing thermal resistance profile compared to 2D baseline

Silicon logic layer thinning from 100 µm to 5 µm to enable nTSV interconnects degrades lateral heat spreading; thermal conductivity of thinned logic die drops from 140 W/m·K to 100 W/m·K and exhibits ballistic/quasiballistic phonon scattering effects below 100 µm, causing 6.7% temperature rise in logic die and 3.1% in memory die

Addition of low thermal conductivity BEOL stack layer (1.2 W/m·K, 2.85 µm thickness) between dies increases thermal resistance path from logic layer to heatsink, raising logic die temperature 3°C higher than memory die despite identical power per unit area

Paper uses lumped thermal RC network model in HotSpot v7.0 which assumes uniform power density within functional blocks; does not resolve sub-block spatial heterogeneity or account for detailed 3D heat flow coupling across nTSV interfaces and F2F bonding uniformity

Steady-state thermal analysis only; no transient thermal coupling effects, thermal cycling fatigue, or dynamic workload variations modeled despite multi-core activity pattern sensitivity demonstrated in Section III.C

studio_assumptions: Ambient temperature fixed at 27°C (representative value for domain)

Thermal design power (TDP) baseline of 40 W for 2D-SOC applies directly to 3D-SOC power scaling analysis; 3D power consumption reduced by 0.913× due to shorter interconnects but power density increased by 1.37× due to footprint reduction by 0.665×
C4 micro-bumps and solder balls replaced with single equivalent thermal conductivity stack (1.25 and 16.67 W/m·K effective)
Face-to-face (F2F) wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding pitch maintained at full 6-metal-layer stack (M6M6, 12 layers) with effective thermal conductivity of F2F via layer
Polymer thermal interface material (PTIM) properties: 100 µm thickness, 7 W/m·K constant thermal conductivity independent of thickness or pressure
Heat spreader and heatsink convective resistance values: 0.17 K/W (heatsink to ambient), 50 K/W (PCB to ambient) remain constant across 2D and 3D configurations
Silicon thermal conductivity values: memory die 140 W/m·K (100 µm), logic die 100 W/m·K (5 µm) assumed isotropic and thickness-dependent per Figure 5(b) ballistic scattering model
Tile-level power breakdown (Figure 3: cores 39%, interconnects 27%, I$ 13%, SPM 11%, others 10%) representative of full 256-core, 64-tile MemPool architecture under full workload
All thermal coupling between logic and memory dies in 3D stacking treated as one-dimensional resistance path through BEOL stack; no lateral heat spreading between dies modeled

methods.note: Paper employs HotSpot v7.0 thermal simulator with lumped RC network model validated against ANSYS commercial FEA tool and experimental thermal test chip [48]. Steady-state thermal analysis methodology clearly described in Section III. However, critical limitation: tool assumes uniform power density within functional blocks and does not resolve transient coupling or sub-block spatial heterogeneity. Tile activity pattern methodology (P1-P4 synthetic patterns from prior work [38]) is sound but patterns themselves not provided in this paper, limiting reproducibility.

code.note: No thermal simulation code, HotSpot configuration files (.flp, .config), floorplan definitions, or model netlists provided. Paper references HotSpot v7.0 repository link [45] but does not archive or document custom MemPool configuration. Detailed floorplan x,y coordinates for tile placement in Figure 9 are qualitative diagrams without exact numerical block positions. Cannot independently verify RC network topology or power density assignments per block.

parameters.note: Critical physical contradiction: Logic die thermal conductivity stated as 100 W/m·K at 5 µm thickness (Table I, Section III.B). However, Figure 5(b) phonon scattering model shows silicon kth drops sharply below 100 µm due to ballistic/quasiballistic effects. At 5 µm (50× thinner), kth should be far lower than 100 W/m·K based on same reference [43] cited for scattering. Paper uses 100 W/m·K as constant value without justifying deviation from Figure 5(b) curve. Additionally, paper states BEOL stack effective kth = 1.2 W/m·K sourced from [42] (Macro-3D) but [42] is not accessed to verify this value independently. F2F via layer (2.85 µm) thermal conductivity not physically derived; appears to be lumped effective value without justification for via pitch, density, or metal trace routing impact.

config.note: Package and floorplan configuration lacks critical details: (1) nTSV (nano-Through-Silicon-Via) density, pitch, and individual thermal conductivity not specified; F2F bonding defect density and delamination risk not modeled. (2) C4 micro-bumps and solder balls replaced with 'single equivalent thermal conductivity stack' (Section II) – this lumping obscures spatial non-uniformity and contact resistance variability. (3) Polymer TIM material property assumed constant (7 W/m·K, 100 µm) independent of contact pressure, temperature, or material aging; no sensitivity analysis provided. (4) Tile floorplan details deferred to [38] and [41]; intermediate floorplan states for SPM capacities 1-8 MiB in Figure 9 lack x,y block coordinates. (5) No specification of which tiles dissipate which power fractions in 3D stack; power distribution assumed uniform per tile type but actual per-block power map not provided.

data.note: Baseline 2D-SOC thermal design power (TDP) of 40 W stated without independent derivation or citation; paper asserts this is for 'larger workloads' but does not specify actual core activity, clock frequency, or voltage. Power density increases to 1.37× in 3D are computed correctly from footprint scaling (0.665×) and power scaling (0.913×), but underlying per-block power values (39% cores, 27% interconnects, etc., Figure 3) are cited from [40] MemPool DATE 2021 paper, not independently validated here. Critical contradiction in MemPool-3D8MiB case (Section IV.C): paper states I$ block moves to logic die, increasing logic die power density from prior 3D configurations, but Figure 10(b) normalized data originates from [41] (arXiv 2112.01168) which is unpublished preprint – no stable reference or independent verification. Workload activity patterns P1-P4 cited from [38] but actual synthetic power/thermal traces not reproduced in this paper; cannot verify pattern definitions or activity coefficients. Temperature measurement results (46°C 2D baseline, 55°C memory 3D, 57°C logic 3D) are HotSpot simulation outputs but validation against experimental hardware or independent solver limited to ANSYS comparison [47] without reported error margins or worst-case bounds.

findings.reason: Table I and Section III.B state logic die kth = 100 W/m·K at 5 µm thickness. However, Figure 5(b) phonon scattering model [43] shows silicon kth should decrease sharply below 100 µm due to ballistic and quasiballistic scattering. At 5 µm (50× below 100 µm threshold), Figure 5(b) trend predicts kth << 100 W/m·K, contradicting the constant 100 W/m·K value used in thermal model. No explanation provided for deviation from own cited reference curve.
findings.locator: Table I page 3; Section III.B page 4-5 'The thermal conductivity for silicon in the memory die and logic die are 140 and 100 W m−1 K −1'; Figure 5(b) page 5 showing steep kth decline below 100 µm

findings.reason: BEOL stack effective thermal conductivity of 1.2 W/m·K (2.85 µm) cited as design parameter from [42] (Bamberg et al. Macro-3D DATE 2020) but [42] is not accessed or independently validated in this review. Value combines metal layers (M6M6, ~10 W/m·K) and dielectric (SiO2, ~1.4 W/m·K) but no derivation shown for 1.2 W/m·K effective value. Proportional mixing rule not confirmed. F2F via layer individual via thermal resistance and via-to-via spacing not specified.
findings.locator: Table I page 3 'BEOL stack... Thermal conductivity 1.2'; Section II page 2-3 'F2F via layer of thickness 2.85 µm [42]'

findings.reason: Section II states 'we have replaced the C4 and solder balls with a single stack of layer with their equivalent thermal conductivities.' This lumping hides spatial non-uniformity in bump pitch (~100-200 µm), underfill filler particle distribution, and solder ball reflow voids. Effective thermal conductivity values (C4: 1.25 W/m·K, solder: 16.67 W/m·K from Table I) are not independently justified. No sensitivity analysis on lumpification accuracy or voiding impact provided.
findings.locator: Section II page 3 'In our thermal modeling study, we have replaced the C4 and solder balls with a single stack of layer with their equivalent thermal conductivities'; Table I page 3 showing equivalent kth values

findings.reason: Paper assumes 40 W baseline TDP for 2D-SOC 'for larger workloads' without deriving this from core count (256), frequency, voltage, or activity. Citation [40] MemPool DATE 2021 is referenced for architecture but TDP source not explicitly stated. Power breakdown percentages (Figure 3: 39% cores, 27% interconnects, 13% I$, 11% SPM) are cited from [40] and [41] but not independently calculated or validated for 28 nm technology or 256-core configuration in this paper.
findings.locator: Section II page 3 'We also assume that the thermal design power (TDP) of the 2D-SOC is 40 W (for larger workloads) as a base line for thermal performance comparative study [38]'; Figure 3 page 3 caption referencing [40]

findings.reason: Figure 9 shows qualitative memory die and logic die floorplans for SPM capacities 1-8 MiB with tile footprint scaling factors but no x,y coordinate maps for individual SPM macros, I$ blocks, or core clusters. Paper states 'Detailed floorplan information of the Memopool 2D-SOC architecture is given in [38]' and 3D floorplan details deferred to [41]. Cannot verify that same-scenario power constraints are met (e.g., all SPM blocks in memory die dissipate consistent power density in 3D configuration vs. 2D tile-level distribution).

findings.reason: Section III.C investigates four tile activity patterns (P1, P2, P3, P4) claimed to optimize thermal performance under 50% workload. Patterns are sourced from [38] but actual synthetic power traces, duty cycles, or activity coefficients are not reproduced in this paper. Cannot independently verify pattern definitions, spatial distribution of active tiles, or reproducibility of optimality claims for P4 (2D) and P3 (3D).
findings.locator: Section III.C page 5 'The case study is performed under 50% workload with four different tile activity patterns (P1, P2, P3 and P4) considered in [38]'; Figure 7 page 5 shows results but patterns not defined in paper; Figure 8 page 5 shows temperature maps for P1-P4 without pattern specifications

findings.reason: Paper employs steady-state thermal analysis only. Section III notes 'dynamic localized heating in and among the architectural-level functional blocks' is a concern for multi-core systems but dynamic thermal coupling between logic and memory dies (especially under partial workload transitions) is not modeled. Claim that pattern P3 for 3D is 'optimum' is valid only for steady-state; transient overshoot and thermal time constants not analyzed. This is material for 3D stacks where inter-die heat spreading is significant.
findings.locator: Section III page 4 'However, the tool has some limitations that it assumes uniform power density within a block'; Section III.C page 5 'the tiles/core activity pattern significantly impact the thermal performance'; no transient analysis reported

findings.reason: Section III.B claims 6.7% temperature rise in logic die and 3.1% in memory die due to logic die thinning from 100 µm to 5 µm (Figure 6b). However, Figure 5(b) phonon scattering model predicts much steeper kth degradation at 5 µm than used in RC model. If actual logic die kth << 100 W/m·K (per ballistic scattering), measured thermal resistance increase should be >6.7%, suggesting paper under-estimates thinning impact. Figure 6(a) shows temperature decreases to 100 µm then rises sharply, but no transitional kth function applied in HotSpot model.
findings.locator: Section III.B page 4-5 Figure 6(a) and 6(b); comparison statement 'the silicon logic layer thinning significantly impacts the thermal performance of the 3D-SOC by rising the logic and memory layer temperature by 6.7% and 3.1% respectively'

findings.reason: Section IV.C states die footprint increases 40% for MemPool-3D8MiB (due to only 15 of 16 SPM macros fitting on memory die) compared to MemPool-3D1MiB. However, power increases only ~1.17× (Figure 9 normalized power). This 40% footprint increase is 'very significant' per authors but Figure 10(a) shows power density for 3D8MiB is 66% higher than 2D8MiB despite footprint scaling up. Logic die power density also increases due to I$ block relocation. Paper does not clearly explain whether this footprint jump represents a design error or intentional trade-off, nor does it justify why 8MiB capacity is practical given thermal performance degradation (44% Tmax increase per abstract).
findings.locator: Section IV.C page 6 'the memory die is occupied by only 15 out of 16 SPM macros with 5×3 array with nearly 100% utilization. This also increases the die footprint by 40% compared to the MemPool-3D1M iB which is very significant'; Figure 10(a) page 6 showing 66% power density increase for 3D8MiB

findings.reason: Paper concludes MOL is optimal for 1-4 MiB and LOM for 8 MiB (Section V). However, no clear design principle or thermal criterion is articulated for when to switch configurations. The 8 MiB case shows LOM improves logic die temperature by 11% but increases memory die temperature by <1%, suggesting the crossover is driven by logic die proximity to heatsink rather than system-level thermal optimization. No guidance provided for other SPM capacities (3, 5, 6, 7 MiB) or scaling to larger dies.
findings.locator: Section V page 7-8 'the simulation results reveals that the thermal issues can be mitigated in the proposed MemPool 3D-SOC with MOL configuration for SPM L1 capacity of 1MiB, 2MiB and 4MiB, and with LOM configuration for SPM L1 capacity of 8MiB'; Figure 12 page 7 showing thermal comparisons

findings.reason: Paper validates HotSpot v7.0 against ANSYS FEA [47] and experimental thermal test chip [48] but does not report error margins, worst-case bounds, or applicability to this specific 3D MemPool design. No silicon measurements from fabricated MemPool die (2D or 3D) provided. Thermal model assumptions (uniform power per tile, effective TIM properties, nTSV density) not experimentally verified. ANSYS validation likely performed on different die geometry; applicability to 3.95×3.95 mm MemPool dies with 64 fine-grained tiles not confirmed.
findings.locator: Section III page 4 'The HotSpot thermal tool is validated against commercial tool ANSYS [47] which is a detailed finite element simulator for 3D heat flow. The HotSpot modeling method is also validated by comparing with a commercial thermal testing chip [48]'; no error margins or applicability statement provided

findings.reason: Figure 10(a) normalizes 3D power density to 2D1MiB baseline and shows 37% increase for 3D1MiB, rising to 66% for 3D8MiB. However, Figure 10(b) normalizes logic and memory die power density for 3D-only configurations (not against 2D baseline). This dual normalization makes it difficult to track absolute power density trends and verify that higher SPM capacities do not violate power density constraints for device reliability (HCD, BTI, TDDB mentioned in abstract but not quantified).

assessment.summary: Paper W4387010219 examines thermal performance of a MemPool RISC-V 256-core multicore SOC in 2D versus 3D configurations using HotSpot v7.0. The scenario describes a 2D baseline with Tmax=46°C and a 3D Memory-on-Logic (MOL) stack showing Tmax=55°C (memory die) and 57°C (logic die), representing +20% and +24% increases respectively at 40W TDP in 28nm technology. Studio execution was skipped due to input validation failures: the floorplan specifies non-power-generating layers (BEOL_Stack, TIM, Heat_Spreader, Heatsink) without assigned power values, and Memory_Die and Logic_Die lack explicit power assignments. Floorplan and power block names do not align. Geometric overlap exists between Logic_Die and BEOL_Stack. No transient trace is available; this is a steady-state 2D-only screening analysis. Verdicts classified as illustrative_2d_only because the custom 2D steady scenario cannot execute without power allocation corrections.
limitations: Input gate failed: all passive/coupling layers (BEOL_Stack, TIM, Heat_Spreader, Heatsink) require finite power values in range [0, 10000] W, but none were assigned. Active layers (Memory_Die, Logic_Die) also lack explicit power fields despite power breakdown available for Cores, Interconnects, Instruction_Cache, SPM, and Others.

Floorplan layer names (Memory_Die, Logic_Die, BEOL_Stack, TIM, Heat_Spreader, Heatsink) do not match power assignment block names (Cores, Interconnects, Instruction_Cache, SPM, Others); mapping between physical geometry and power distribution is undefined.
Geometric collision: BEOL_Stack and Logic_Die occupy overlapping coordinates (y_m from 0.00395 to 0.00395), violating non-overlap constraint required for 3D thermal solver initialization.

Scientific gate failed: Evidence citations lack valid page numbers and pinned asset locators (all evidence items report null asset_id and missing page validation). Evidence sha256 differs from expected value, indicating unverified or modified extraction.

No HotSpot v7.0 configuration files (.flp, .config) available; model files not publicly archived or linked in supplementary materials. Floorplan and power input must be reconstructed from Figure 3, Figure 4, and Table I text descriptions rather than from machine-readable source.

Physical mismatches identified as essential: (1) 3D MOL configuration reduces footprint by 0.665× but increases power density by 1.37× relative to 2D, altering thermal resistance profile; (2) logic die thinning from 100 µm to 5 µm reduces thermal conductivity from 140 to 100 W/m·K and introduces ballistic phonon scattering causing +6.7% logic die temperature rise and +3.1% secondary memory die rise; (3) low-κ BEOL stack layer (1.2 W/m·K, 2.85 µm) adds 3°C temperature differential between logic and memory dies. These effects cannot be validated without solving 3D coupled transport.

Lumped RC network model (HotSpot v7.0) assumes uniform power density within functional blocks and treats 3D die coupling as 1D resistance chain. Does not resolve sub-block spatial heterogeneity, nTSV contact resistance distribution, or F2F bonding defect density; 3D heat flow through via arrays is collapsed to effective thermal conductivity.

Steady-state only analysis; no transient thermal response, dynamic workload switching between tiles (P1–P4 patterns in Section III.C), or thermal cycling fatigue modeled. Multi-core activity patterns reported as qualitative sensitivity study without quantified time-domain coupling.

Candidate 40 W TDP baseline for 2D-SOC not independently derived or validated in this paper; value sourced from prior MemPool design [38] without re-measurement. Power scaling factors (0.913× for 3D total power, 1.37× for 3D power density) are design projections, not measured.

Thermal conductivity of thinned 5 µm logic layer (100 W/m·K) sourced from ballistic phonon scattering model [43] (Vermeersch et al. APL 2016) but not independently validated experimentally. No silicon test wafer measurements provided.

Polymer TIM properties (100 µm, 7 W/m·K) treated as constant; contact resistance, thickness variability, and delamination effects under thermal cycling not modeled. Material variability not quantified.

Face-to-face via layer thermal conductivity (effective 1.2 W/m·K) cited from [42] (Bamberg et al. DATE 2020); individual via pitch, density, and metal trace routing not specified. nTSV contact resistance and F2F bonding uniformity not characterized.

Comparison_valid flag is false; numerical values (46°C baseline, 55°C memory die, 57°C logic die) cannot be independently validated or reproduced without corrected floorplan geometry, aligned power assignments, and access to HotSpot model files. Simulation was blocked and did not run.
